samples.summary: New PR-facing panel channel (`agent-deferred-findings` check run) is recorded in no design doc — only in a task todo
samples.evidence: CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 requires a feature / non-trivial change to "write or update a design doc under docs/design/" and to include it in the PR; CONTRIBUTING.md:57-61 says to update the existing doc for the area. `docs/design/harness-engineering.md` is that canonical doc for the review panel and documents every existing channel in detail — the per-lens `agent-review-<lens>` check run and the `output.text`/carry-forward contract (lines 1609-1655), the infra-error exclusion (1657-1675), and even sibling modules by name (`prior-findings.mjs` 1649, `panel-job-summary.mjs` 1092, `fix-brief.mjs` 2859). The diff adds a second check run written on every panel run, a new JSON wire format (`agent-deferred-findings/v1`), a new naming invariant tied to `set-state.mjs`'s prefix scan, and a new rubric-generation stamp — none of it appears in any file under docs/design/. Grepping docs/ for "deferred-findings" matches only `docs/tasks/active/20260825-deferred-findings-channel-todo.md`, which is an execution plan, not a design doc. Two existing statements in the doc also go stale: line 1051 ("the autonomous panel recorded verdicts only as `agent-review-*` check runs") and the channel inventory at 1116-1122.

samples.summary: `always()` makes the advisory record fire on cancelled/superseded and crashed panels, writing "None this round" for a round that produced no verdicts
samples.evidence: Both new steps are gated on `always() && steps.pr.outputs.number != ''` (workflow lines 1089 and 1114), while the immediately preceding "Post per-lens check runs" is deliberately `!cancelled()` — the comment at lines 889-905 and the design doc's cancellation traps (harness-engineering.md:1990-2000, "`stalled` moved from `always()` to `!cancelled()`") explain why a superseded run must not write PR-visible records. On a cancelled or crashed run `.agent-review/<lens>/verdict.json` is absent for every lens, so `readLensFindings` returns nothing, `buildDeferredCheck` emits `total: 0`, and the check reports "None this round." — precisely the statement the task plan calls a lie in its own fail-direction table (`lenses.json` unreadable ⇒ refuse, because "an empty record would read as 'this round deferred nothing'"). The module cannot distinguish "nothing deferred" from "the panel never ran", and the workflow gate is what hands it that case.

samples.summary: Advisory check is always `checks.create`, never an update, so re-runs on one head sha leave duplicate contradictory records
samples.evidence: The lens path deliberately prefers `checks.update` on the in-progress run (workflow lines 1043-1058) because two panels on one sha produced "twelve check runs for six lenses, last writer wins" (harness-engineering.md:1979-1988). The new step unconditionally calls `github.rest.checks.create` with `head_sha: context.payload.workflow_run.head_sha`, so a CI re-run or `@claude rerun` on the same commit accumulates several `agent-deferred-findings` runs with different totals and no way for a reader (or the eventual consumer this archive is being built for) to tell which is current.

samples.summary: The deferred-population rule is a third copy of the gating filter rather than being derived from the existing one, so the two channels can silently disagree
samples.evidence: `isDeferred` re-encodes the gate as `!BLOCKING.has(normalizeSeverity(...)) || lane === 'backlog'`. The same rule already exists twice: inline in the workflow's gating projection (`.filter(critical|major).filter(f => f.lane !== 'backlog')`, agent-review-panel.yml:998-1000, with its own local `norm`) and as `gatingFindings` in `scripts/agent/review-panel.mjs:929-936`. The module's header claims "It reads the same file the gating channel reads, so the two cannot disagree about what the round found" — but they can: widening or narrowing either filter (e.g. persisting `minor` in `output.text`) makes a finding appear in both channels or neither, with nothing binding them. Exporting the complement of `gatingFindings` (or moving the predicate into `severity.mjs`, where the "what blocks a PR" single source of truth already lives) would make the two projections structurally inseparable.

samples.summary: The task plan for this change is not in the tasks index (`pnpm tasks:index` not re-run)
samples.evidence: `docs/tasks/active/20260825-deferred-findings-channel-todo.md` exists on the branch, but `docs/tasks/README.md`'s Active Tasks table lists only `20260825-frontend-vite-config-node-floor-todo.md` for that date and no deferred-findings row; "Latest active task" (line 48) is also stale. docs/tasks/README.md:9 states the index is regenerated with `pnpm tasks:index`, and no verification lane covers docs/tasks (verify-doc-index.mjs contains no 'tasks'/'active' reference), so nothing else will catch it.

verdict.reason: The absence is real. A repo-wide grep for `deferred-findings`/`deferredFindings` matches only the new module (`scripts/agent/deferred-findings.mjs`), its test, `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml`, other reviewers' `.agent-review/` output, and `docs/tasks/active/20260825-deferred-findings-channel-todo.md`. Broader greps over `docs/design/**` for `deferred`, `deferred findings`, `advisory check`, `non-blocking`, `panel_sha`, `noveltyOrigin`, `surfaceScope` turn up nothing about this channel; the four `deferred` hits in harness-engineering.md (634, 979, 1689, 3104) are unrelated. I enumerated every file under docs/design/ — there is no panel/review-channel doc other than harness-engineering.md, which docs/design/README.md:163-164 identifies as the canonical harness design doc (hunter-usage.md is described as its operator guide). The change itself is genuinely a new PR-facing channel with a versioned wire contract and a naming invariant (deferred-findings.mjs:62, 73, 93, 99; agent-review-panel.yml:1070-1126, including a third `checks.create`), i.e. an architecture-level addition. CONTRIBUTING.md:13-16 and 57-61 are quoted accurately and require updating the existing area doc; CONTRIBUTING.md:62-65 classifies the todo file as an execution plan, not a design doc. Two doc statements also go stale (harness-engineering.md:1050-1051 "recorded verdicts ONLY as `agent-review-*` check runs"; the channel/module inventory at 1088-1129). Under this lens's rubric, a missing/unupdated design doc for an architecture change is a `major` fit violation, so the finding is blocking.

verdict.reason: The claimed code is present exactly as described: both new steps are gated on always() (agent-review-panel.yml:1089 and :1114) while the immediately preceding verdict-writing step is deliberately !cancelled() (:926-927, rationale comment at :889-905). On a cancelled/superseded run no .agent-review/<lens>/verdict.json exists, so readLensFindings skips every lens (deferred-findings.mjs:378-393), collectDeferred returns [] (:201-211), buildDeferredText emits total: 0 (:234-266) and renderDeferredSummary prints "None this round." (:272-283) — a PR-visible advisory record asserting nothing was deferred for a round that produced no verdicts, created against the superseded head sha (:1132). The module cannot distinguish "nothing deferred" from "the panel never ran"; its only refusal path is an unreadable lenses.json (main, :406-415). This conflicts with the documented cancellation invariant in the subsystem design doc (harness-engineering.md:1929-1933 and :1990-2000) and with the change's own fail-direction table (docs/tasks/active/20260825-deferred-findings-channel-todo.md:132), and the plan concedes the wiring was never exercised against a live panel run (:176-179). Mitigations (neutral conclusion, name outside the agent-review- prefix that set-state.mjs reads, continue-on-error) bound the blast radius but do not make the record truthful, and I am not certain enough that a deviation from a documented subsystem invariant falls outside the design-fit lane to drop the finding. No refutation ground established.
